pr_title: Fix: Inclusion of DateTime in a Date range and vice versa
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/36175 which exists for Rails 5.2.3 and Rails 6, too.

With this fix, the range inclusion predicate method works as intended.

```ruby
(Date.today.beginning_of_month..Date.today.end_of_month).include?(Date.today) # => true
(Date.today.beginning_of_month..Date.today.end_of_month).include?(DateTime.now) # => true
(DateTime.now.beginning_of_month..DateTime.now.end_of_month).include?(Date.today) # => true
(DateTime.now.beginning_of_month..DateTime.now.end_of_month).include?(DateTime.now) # => true
```

@vishaltelangre I've opened an issue report on Ruby to check if the change should be done at Ruby level instead: https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/16440

In the meantime, I think the PR looks good. Can you squash your commits so once they make the call it can easily be merged?

[Range#include?](https://ruby-doc.org/core-2.6.5/Range.html#method-i-include-3F) in Ruby checks if the argument is one of the _members_ of the range-as-a-sequence, e.g. if `Range#to_a` will include it.
To check whether the argument is in the space between `begin` and `end`, [Range#cover?](https://ruby-doc.org/core-2.6.5/Range.html#method-i-cover-3F) should be used.

I believe this kind of "edge case hacks", even if they look good on one particular example, are in fact harmful (for AS users) because of muddying the underlying Ruby semantics.

issue_context.title: DateTime, Date comparison doesn't work as expected
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

```ruby
may1 = Date.today.beginning_of_month # => Wed, 01 May 2019
may31 = Date.today.end_of_month # => Fri, 31 May 2019

(may1..may31).include? Date.today # => True
(may1..may31).include? DateTime.now # => False
```

### Expected behavior
`(may1..may31).include? DateTime.now` should return `True` for DateTime's in the same month

### Actual behavior
It returns `False`

### System configuration
**Rails version**: Rails 5.2.3

**Ruby version**: ruby 2.6.0p0 (2018-12-25 revision 66547) [x86_64-linux]
comments:
You are trying to compare `DateTime` against `Date`. Your example will work if you change your last expectation with:

```ruby
(may1..may31).include? DateTime.now.to_date
```
I realize that, but my expectation was that DateTime comparison with Date should Just Work

I feel this is an issue for Ruby itself.
Can you file an issue on https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/ ?

This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has not been commented on for at least three months.
The resources of the Rails team are limited, and so we are asking for your help.
If you can still reproduce this error on the `5-2-stable` branch or on `master`, please reply with all of the information you have about it in order to keep the issue open.
Thank you for all your contributions.
@kamipo I created https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/16440 for this issue

Actually, if the purpose is to check if the given date range covers a specific Date or Datetime, I think [`Range#cover?`](https://ruby-doc.org/core-2.6.4/Range.html#method-i-cover-3F) should be a better API to use.

The grey area of `Range#include?` is that we're not sure if it should treat the date range *a series of individual days*, or *a continuous range between 2 specific times*. This might take some debate to decide. So my suggestion to @yazinsai or anyone that comes across this issue is to just use `Range#cover?` ;-)

review_comments: @rafaelfranca That's what this PR does. We rely on `#cover?` here. This fix is inspired by this extension https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/870f087825/activesupport/lib/active_support/core_ext/range/include_time_with_zone.rb which is already present in the upstream.

I'm more inclined to remove that extension. `include?` should not work for values that `Range.to_a` would not return.

Can we deprecate that extension and tell people to use `cover?` instead?
@rafaelfranca Sure. I will make another PR to deprecate the `activesupport/lib/active_support/core_ext/range/include_time_with_zone.rb` extension.

Should also add test cases for `Time` inclusion. Like:

```ruby
(Date.yesterday..Date.tomorrow).include?(Time.now)
(Date.yesterday..Date.tomorrow).include?(Time.zone.now)
```
Added tests for these scenarios, too.
